arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Puckett's lawyer argued the government broke a clear promise. He stated this breach caused prejudice at sentencing.
The government's lawyer argued objections serve important court functions. She claimed Puckett's silence forfeited his claim.
Justice Roberts noted remorse is theoretically consistent with future crimes. He questioned the logic of the plea terms.
Justice Alito asked if the judge knew the facts from the presentence report. He probed the necessity of the objection.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Puckett pled guilty. The government promised a sentence reduction. They failed to recommend it. Puckett did not object at trial. He now appeals. The Court must decide if he can still win.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the remedy for broken plea deals. It determines whether defendants must object immediately to preserve their rights. It shapes how federal courts handle government breaches of trust.
